reasons: 화풍: 윤곽이 근흑(재질 어두운 톤 아님) (4/4)

answer.evidence: The cargo box has a light roof band on rows 2-12 (x=48 and x=70 at L~230-234). It ends in a lighter edge line at row 13 (L=202), then darker eave shadow on rows 14-15 (L=162, 119), and the vertical side panel with stripe ribs runs below from row 16 to about row 42. The cab has the same structure at x=25: a light roof band on rows 14-23, an edge line at row 24 and shadow at row 25, then the windshield and door face below. The truck is drawn in left-facing profile as its south face, which is normal. The wheels are small details and do not count against the body.

styleAnswer.evidence: The truck's cargo box is a large white/grey panel with only a few vertical seam lines and a soft top highlight, so it reads as a flat fill. 45% near-flat coverage against 0-13% for the references confirms this. The cab, bumper and wheels have 2-3 steps each, with no grain, speckle or per-part shading. The dark edge pixels are 88% near-neutral, so the outline is a uniform near-black line rather than a tint of the neighbouring material. That is the sticker look, unlike the tinted outlines of the hedge (0%) and cheese stall (1%). It has 7 visible tones per tile, below the hedge (9), stall (17) and well (20). The wheels and cab windows are cleanly drawn but simple. A careful artist would find it flatter and thinner than the references.

styleAnswer.evidence: The truck has a large white cargo box with only 2-3 steps (white, light grey, a few panel lines). Its flat panels and cab body are mostly one colour. The outline and dark edges are 88% near-neutral, so it reads as a neutral black/grey sticker line, unlike the tinted dark-material outlines on the hedge, stall and well. styleAnswer.evidence: The truck's cargo box and cab are large areas of near-flat white/grey with only a few vertical panel lines, and 45% of the piece is near-flat against 0-13% for the references that measure it. The box ramp has roughly 3 steps (white, light grey, grey) against about 5-6 on the references. The dark edge pixels are 88% near-neutral, so the outline is a neutral near-black line around the wheels, cab and box, which gives the sticker look. The references use tinted dark tones (hedge 0%, stall 1%). It has 7 visible tones per tile, below the stall (17) and well (20) and comparable only to the simplest references. It has no grain, speckle, or per-panel highlights like the stall and well. The bench and lamp have no per-tile facts, but by eye they are thin and not comparable. Overall it reads as a clean but shallow, flat-filled vehicle and falls short of the Beodeul bar.

answer.evidence: The truck faces left, so its south face is the side profile, which is normal. The cargo box, the largest volume, has a light top band at rows 2-12 (about 11 rows, L≈230-245). styleAnswer.evidence: The truck's cargo box is a big near-white panel with only a few vertical seam lines and a faint edge shade, so it reads as 2-3 lightness steps against the references' 5-6. The cab is also flat: pale body, a blue window and dark wheels with little modelling. Dark edge pixels are 88% near-neutral, which fits the uniform dark grey/black outline of the sticker look; the references are tinted (hedge 0%, stall 1%, well 33%). Near-flat coverage is 45% against 0-13% in the references, so large areas are flat fills with no grain, speckle or dirt. The candidate has 7 visible tones per tile, against 9-20 for the hedge, stall and well. The truck is cleanly drawn and the proportions are readable, but it is flatter and more sticker-like than the Beodeul standard.
